title: Rerank endpoint: vector-store eviction + compaction interaction caused throughput and quality regression postmortem
creator: Maya Chen
incident_summary: On 2025-03-05 we observed a sustained degradation in rerank throughput and a concurrent drop in top-1 rerank quality for a subset of customers. The root cause was an interaction between the vector-store background shard compaction job and the inference KV cache eviction policy which forced frequent safety-fallback model routing and increased tail latency. The issue lasted ~18 hours for the affected shard pool until mitigations were applied.
timeline: 2025-03-05T02:12Z - First automated alert: rerank endpoint p95 latency increased from 90ms to 420ms for shard-pool-us-west-2-b.
2025-03-05T02:18Z - Oncall engineer (Diego) acknowledged and started triage. Error rate unchanged but throughput decreased 25% on the pool.
2025-03-05T02:35Z - Quick inspection of node metrics showed increased CPU and GPU memory churn on indexer nodes; compaction jobs were running at higher frequency than expected.
2025-03-05T03:05Z - Discovered repeated vector-store shard eviction logs: service was evicting cached prefixes with an LRU that didn't account for active re-ranking sessions.

2025-03-05T03:40Z - Correlation found between compaction start times and KV cache misses; missing KV cache entries triggered fallback to quantized model variant with slightly lower quality and higher compute per token.

2025-03-05T04:15Z - Emergency mitigation: paused background compaction on affected shard pool and increased KV cache size for the pool by 30% via runtime flag. Immediate p95 latency improved from 420ms to 140ms.
2025-03-05T05:00Z - Validation: ran replay tests on canary traffic for 2 hours; rerank precision@1 returned to baseline for most queries but some long-prefix queries still showed variability.
2025-03-05T09:00Z - Rolled a staged config change: decouple compaction scheduling from the heavy write window and enabled soft-locks to prevent eviction of active prefix ranges.
2025-03-05T20:00Z - Back to steady state metrics; post-incident monitoring kept compaction off for 24 hours and then resumed at reduced concurrency.
2025-03-12T10:00Z - Postmortem writeup completed and long-term fixes scheduled.
root_cause: A misalignment between the vector-store compaction scheduler and the inference KV cache eviction policy caused active prefix entries to be evicted while compaction reclaimed index space. Evicted prefixes led to cache misses during rerank requests, which triggered automatic model routing to a quantized fallback variant. The fallback increased per-request compute and returned slightly lower ranking precision for certain query patterns. Two contributing factors: (1) compaction concurrency default was recently increased in ENG-20650 to speed maintenance; (2) the KV cache LRU algorithm did not mark in-flight rerank prefixes as protected, causing premature eviction.
technical_details:
- Vector store compaction reclaims tombstoned vectors and rewrites shard segments; rewritten segments temporarily change shard layout and cause transient key lookups to miss if prefix locking isn't used.
- KV cache keys include prefix hashes; eviction used global LRU with a 5-minute TTL and no concept of active session pins.
- Model routing rule: if KV cache miss rate for a request exceeds 40% we route to quantized-alt model (lower VRAM) to preserve capacity. This routing threshold was reached for high-prefix-volume customers.
- Observed metrics: p95 latency spike correlated with KV cache miss rate jumping from 8% to 62%; throughput dropped 18-32% across affected hosts.
- No data corruption observed; integrity checks passed for rewritten shards.
mitigation_and_actions_taken: 1) Immediately paused background compaction on affected pools. 2) Increased KV cache allocation for shard-pool-us-west-2-b by 30% via runtime override. 3) Lowered quantized fallback routing aggressiveness from 40% to 70% miss-rate as temporary safety. 4) Deployed a hotfix to mark active rerank sessions as pinned in the cache for 90s to avoid eviction during compaction windows. 5) Notified impacted customers and returned detailed incident timelines and mitigations.
metrics_impact:
- Peak p95 latency increased from ~90ms to 420ms.
- Average throughput for affected pool decreased ~25% during the incident window.
- KV cache miss rate rose from 8% baseline to 62% at peak.
- Top-1 rerank precision dropped ~6 percentage points for long-prefix queries on affected customers.
customer_impact_details: Medium impact for a small cohort of customers (5 customers on the affected shard pool) who reported slowed rerank responses and subtle quality regressions in search results for long context queries. No data loss. Some customers observed higher cost due to additional model compute from fallback routing.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-20910 - Implement compaction-aware cache pinning for all rerank pools (priority P0, estimate 5)
ENG-20911 - Add compaction concurrency safety limits and adaptive backoff to compaction scheduler (priority P1, estimate 3)
ENG-20912 - Revisit model fallback routing thresholds and add gradual degrade policy instead of binary switch (priority P1, estimate 5)
ENG-20913 - Add runbook playbook for compaction-related latency incidents and update oncall docs (priority P2, estimate 2)
ENG-20914 - Improve observability: expose prefix-level cache eviction traces and compaction overlap heatmaps in Console (priority P1, estimate 4)
retrospective_notes: Primary lesson: maintenance jobs (compaction) must be scheduled with awareness of live inference workloads. The separation of concerns between indexer maintenance and inference cache semantics led to incorrect assumptions. We need better cross-team signals and automated safeguards: compaction should consider active session pins and our cache policy should support per-session pinning so live traffic isn't penalized. Also, routing fallbacks that affect output quality should be progressively degraded with feedback rather than binary switches. Action items above track the required engineering and observability work.
communication_and_notifications:
- Customer-facing incident summary sent to affected customers on 2025-03-06.
- Internal incident review held 2025-03-07 with PMs and SREs.
- Slack channel #incidents-embeddings used for real-time updates; postmortem posted to #postmortems and distributed to CTO and Head of Product.
